exodus.10.p1.b1.text: Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials, that I may perform these miraculous signs of Mine among them,

exodus.10.p1.b2.text: and that you may tell your children and grandchildren how severely I dealt with the Egyptians … so that all of you may know that I am the LORD.

exodus.10.p1.b3.text: How long will you refuse to humble yourself before Me? Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.

exodus.10.p1.b4.text: I will bring locusts into your territory tomorrow. They will cover the face of the land so that no one can see it …

exodus.10.p2.b5.text: How long will this man be a snare to us? … Do you not yet realize that Egypt is in ruins?

exodus.10.p2.b6.text: Go, worship the LORD your God … But who exactly will be going?

exodus.10.p2.b7.text: We will go with our young and old … We will go with our sons and daughters, and with our flocks and herds …

exodus.10.p2.b8.text: No, only the men may go and worship the LORD, since that is what you have been requesting.

exodus.10.p3.b9.text: Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, so that the locusts may swarm over it and devour every plant in the land—everything that the hail has left behind.

exodus.10.p3.b10.text: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and throughout that day and night the LORD sent an east wind across the land.

exodus.10.p3.b11.text: By morning the east wind had brought the locusts.

exodus.10.p4.b12.text: The locusts swarmed across the land and settled over the entire territory of Egypt. Never before had there been so many locusts, and never again will there be.

exodus.10.p4.b13.text: They covered the face of all the land until it was black, and they consumed all the plants on the ground and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had left behind.

exodus.10.p4.b14.text: Nothing green was left on any tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.

exodus.10.p5.b15.text: I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.

exodus.10.p5.b16.text: Now please forgive my sin once more and appeal to the LORD your God, that He may remove this death from me.”

exodus.10.p5.b17.text: And the LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind that carried off the locusts and blew them into the Red Sea. Not a single locust remained anywhere in Egypt.

exodus.10.p5.b18.text: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let the Israelites go.

exodus.10.p6.b19.text: Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that darkness may spread over the land of Egypt—a palpable darkness.

exodus.10.p6.b20.text: So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and total darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days.

exodus.10.p6.b21.text: No one could see anyone else, and for three days no one left his place.

exodus.10.p6.b22.text: Yet all the Israelites had light in their dwellings.

exodus.10.p7.b23.text: Go, worship the LORD. Even your little ones may go with you; only your flocks and herds must stay behind.

exodus.10.p7.b24.text: Even our livestock must go with us; not a hoof will be left behind …

exodus.10.p7.b25.text: Depart from me! … Make sure you never see my face again, for on the day you see my face, you will die.

exodus.10.p7.b26.text: As you say … I will never see your face again.
